attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm 'no bailout coming' is a forecast. The revised wording keeps his next-sentence concession that government money would not fix the continuing spending and demand problem.

contract.note: Reading the denial together with its 'even if' concession is a fair plain reading. Treating ordinary procurement as no rescue matches his framing. No deadline was invented.

evidence.note: Official GSA procurement deal dated 2026-09-10 with no spend commitment. This is a government release, not a company one. It is not a rescue, so it neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended negative forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no implemented rescue that sustains the labs' compute spending, so nothing contradicts it. A finite period without a bailout cannot support it either. The outcome stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'It's very obvious that neither of them are done raising billions… in 2026' is a firm forecast about CoreWeave and Nebius. 'At random' is rhetoric.

contract.note: Reading 'billions' as at least $2B per company, after publication and within 2026, is an ordinary reading. Counting an executed credit facility is a stated, reasonable choice; the Nebius result depends on it.

evidence.note: CoreWeave closed a $4.2B convertible notes offering on 2026-09-22. This is after publication and before the evaluation date, and it clears $2B.
Reuters reports Nebius secured a $3.5B Citi facility on 2026-10-22. This is after publication and before the evaluation date. It is an executed facility, which the contract counts.

reviews.rationale: Each company secured more than $2B of new external financing after 2026-08-25 and before the evaluation date: CoreWeave $4.2B in notes, Nebius a $3.5B facility. Under the contract's early-resolution rule, the forecast is supported.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A polemical causal claim that keeps his wording. Parts of it ('suffocated', 'endless growth', 'allowed to annihilate') are rhetoric rather than testable.

contract.note: Reading the claim as at least $200B of cumulative training spend by the two labs, necessity, and material distortion of public understanding is a plain reading. The result turns on readings he did not supply: joint vs individual totals, training scope, and strict necessity.

evidence.note: Epoch/AI Index estimates of annual compute spend through 2025, mixing R&D and inference. These are not training-only and stop before the post date.
DeepSeek-V3's training-run cost estimate covers a different company and excludes prior research. It cannot settle necessity for OpenAI or Anthropic.
A study finding negligible immediate effects of anthropomorphic framing. It does not test cumulative effects or overpromising, so it does not defeat the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable cumulative training-cost figures for OpenAI and Anthropic through August 2026. It also has no decisive evidence on whether the spending was necessary or on industry-wide distortion. The items are context only. The claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The cost clause is a firm forecast. 'Already approaching the limits' is a present-tense judgment folded into the forecast. The universal 'every single data center' is kept.

contract.note: An ordinary reading. Limiting the claim to sites using the repriced systems from 2027 is a mild narrowing that helps the speaker. 'Approaching the limits' has no stated measure.

evidence.note: A pre-publication estimate of at least $5B extra cost for a 1GW site. It is a projection, not a realized budget revision, so it is not evidence of the outcome.
The price rise applies to deliveries in early 2027, so realized cost effects cannot appear before the evaluation date.
A Goldman CEO's pre-post remark that capital is plentiful. It comes from an interested party and predates the claim, so it is not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and the price rise only bites on deliveries from 2027. The packet has no project-level cost revisions and no post-publication financing failures or ceiling. The pre-post estimate and the banker's remark are context. The claim is unresolved.
